answer.evidence: The roof occupies rows 0-28 as a wide trapezoid (width 44 growing to 62) made of door panels laid as a sloped plane, ending in a light edge line at row 28 and followed by a dark brown beam and dark eave shadow at rows 29-33. Below, the front face of stacked pallets with a dark entrance runs rows 34-62 (29 rows). The roof is a sloped plane (evidence c) and the front wall is a separate vertical face, so this reads as a three-quarter view.

styleAnswer.evidence: Measured facts favour the candidate: 18 visible tones per tile against 12 and 10 for the references, 5% near-flat coverage, and 0% neutral dark edge pixels. Its outline is a dark brown that leans toward the wood, not a black sticker line. By eye it is still a smaller and simpler piece than the references. The door roof panels are each close to a single flat tone with a thin highlight and a few speckles, giving roughly 3-4 steps per colour, where the reference tile roofs have 5-6 steps with per-tile highlights. The pallet wall is mostly mid-brown with horizontal plank lines and little per-board grain or variation. The interior is a dark void with a small sack. The tone count is inflated by the four different roof hues, so the shading depth on any single material ramp is shallower than Beodeul. The object sits at the same scale and is cleanly drawn, but it reads a little thinner and flatter than the references.
